- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 3–5 days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–2% for next 3–7 days to avoid underreaction.  
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in the 10–15 day horizon; apply +1.5%–3% bias to forecast for 10–15 day window.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to avoid premature correction.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after spike, model fails to recognize momentum; apply +2%–4% downward bias for 5–10 days post-spike.  
- Model often ignores sentiment shifts in the 1–3 day window; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change within 2–4 days of shift.
